text:
Ava (People Ops): Thanks everyone for joining the all-hands. We'll use this thread for follow-ups re: promotions, leveling, comp, and benefits. Drop Qs and we'll answer live. TL;DR: calibration window opens next week, comp letters mid-June, bonus payout in July.
Elena (CEO): Quick note — promotions are tied to impact + scope. Calibration aims for consistency; leadership will explain decisions after the window. :sparkles:
Sophie L.: Any clarity on concrete criteria for L3 -> L4? What are measurable outputs we can point to?
Raj (VP Eng): For eng, L4 means ownership of cross-team projects, mentoring, and consistent product/metric impact. I'll post a short rubric with examples.
Marcus (CTO): We'll publish a single doc with examples + a FAQ. Targeting EOD Tuesday for the draft.
Daren: If I'm promoted this cycle, when does the salary change happen? Immediate or next payroll?
Jules (Recruiting): Promo raises apply as of the promotion effective date in the notification; payroll timing follows payroll cutoffs. People Ops will confirm per case.
Ava (People Ops): Promo raises take effect on the promotion effective date. Payroll cutoff is the 20th of the month — if the promotion is effective before the cutoff you'll see the change in the next paycheck, otherwise the following.
Kim: Is there a formal appeals process for calibration outcomes? Heard folks ask about this.
Ava (People Ops): Yes. Managers should raise context during calibration. If you think your manager missed material contributions, there will be a calibration appeal window (72 hours after you get the calibration outcome). Send a concise doc to people-ops@redwood.com with evidence.
Elena (CEO): Important: appeals are to surface missing context, not to re-run the entire calibration. Keep them factual and focused.
Sophie L.: How's the budget looking? Any risk to promotions because of hiring constraints?
Raj (VP Eng): No freeze on internal promotions. We're conservative on new hires, but promotions are funded from the compensation pool. If a promotion would require additional headcount funding, we'll review it case-by-case.
Daren: Parental leave — is there flexibility on start date and top-up pay?
Ava (People Ops): Yes, parental leave allows flexible start dates. Salary top-up depends on tenure and role; we'll DM a tailored breakdown and the policy link.
Kim: Any changes to 401(k) match or benefits for next year?
Ava (People Ops): No plan changes for 2026. Match remains 4% up to our annual cap. We're exploring enhancements for 2027.
oncall-bot: Reminder: calibration meeting scheduled 2026-06-08 10:00-12:00 PT.
Marcus (CTO): Sharing an engineering rubric snippet to unblock questions:
```
L4: leads cross-team project, ships impact (measured by product metric), mentors 3+ engineers, defines/owns rollout and reliability
```
Sophie L.: Will the rubric include team-specific examples (frontend/backend/infra)?
Raj (VP Eng): Yes — core behaviors + team-specific examples. We'll surface examples in the doc.
Ava (People Ops): We'll consolidate all Qs into an FAQ and post in #docs/people-ops. If you need confidentiality, DM me or email people-ops@redwood.com. We'll keep this thread open for 48 hrs for any follow-ups. Thanks!
